_comment: Staff-action catalogue (staff access spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-staff-access-design.md §5). Validated at boot by src/staff/catalogue.ts; a malformed entry stops the boot. {name} placeholders come only from validated params and bindings. 'customer order' = a customer's purchase order TO Dearborn Denim (purchase-order-receiver); 'vendor PO' = our purchase order TO a vendor (kanban-purchaser). 'ticket' = a cs-desk customer-service ticket (a retail customer's email thread), never either kind of PO.

inventory_lookup.description: Look up Shopify stock for a product at the Factory and at the Andersonville store. Search by product name, color, size or SKU; returns up to 25 variants with their SKU, levels {factory, store} (null = not stocked at that location), sku_class and whether the product is on POS. Jeans are counted by sub-assembly at each location: all inseams of a style/wash/waist share one count, and setting one sets them all.

q.description: Product name, color, size or SKU, e.g. "H201 hoodie medium".

pos_status.description: Check whether a product is published to the store's POS and which of its variants are stocked at the store. Search by product name, color, size or SKU. Read-only: publishing to POS is Robert's.

q.description: Product name, color, size or SKU.

store_inventory_set.description: Set the on-hand count of one SKU at your store to a counted number (a recount, not a move). Use inventory_lookup first to get the exact SKU. Moving stock between the Factory and the store is inventory_transfer, never this. Jeans are counted by sub-assembly at each location: all inseams of a style/wash/waist share one count, and setting one sets them all. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

quantity.description: The counted quantity now at the store.

reason.description: Why the count changed, e.g. "recount after weekend".

inventory_transfer.description: Record goods physically moved between the Factory and your store: subtracts the quantity at one location and adds it at the other. Jeans are counted by sub-assembly at each location: all inseams of a style/wash/waist share one count, and setting one sets them all. Use inventory_lookup first to get the exact SKU. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

direction.description: to_store = Factory to store; to_factory = store back to the Factory.

reason.description: Why they moved, e.g. "restock for the weekend".

to_store.summary: Move {quantity} × {sku} from the Factory to the store

to_factory.summary: Move {quantity} × {sku} from the store to the Factory

vendor_po_lookup.description: Look up vendor POs: Dearborn Denim's open purchase orders to our vendors (fabric, thread, trims), with each PO's id, PO number, vendor, status and lines, plus pending material requests. Use it to find the vendor PO id before vendor_po_receive. Not for customer orders.

vendor_po_receive.description: Receive materials that arrived from a vendor against a vendor PO (our purchase order to that vendor). Get the vendor PO id and its line ids from vendor_po_lookup first; partial quantities are fine. Never for customer orders. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves.

po_id.description: The vendor PO id from vendor_po_lookup (not the customer order number).

lines.description: What arrived, one entry per PO line: {line_id or sku, quantity, unit?}.

sku.description: Material SKU, when the line id is not known.

unit.description: Unit of the quantity, when it differs from the PO line.

vendor_po_waiting.description: List the vendor POs waiting for Robert's approval: our purchase orders to vendors (fabric, thread, trims) that purchasing drafted and nobody has approved yet, each with its PO number, vendor, total in USD, version (a short code that changes whenever the PO changes), number of lines, when it started waiting and whether it is on hold. vendor narrows the list to one vendor (its code or part of its name); leave it out for every waiting PO. Always call this before vendor_po_approve and show the POs with their totals; approve nothing from memory. Not for customer orders.

vendor.description: Vendor code or part of the vendor name, e.g. "Cone Denim"; leave out for all vendors.

vendor_po_approve.description: Approve vendor POs that are waiting for approval, so purchasing sends them to the vendors (our purchase orders to vendors; an approved vendor PO goes out and cannot be taken back from here). The rule: first call vendor_po_waiting, show the person each PO's number, vendor and total plus the grand total, and only after they confirm call this with exactly those PO numbers and the totals and versions that look-up returned. "Approve all" means every PO the look-up returned; "approve the Cone Denim POs" means every PO the look-up with vendor=Cone Denim returned. A PO marked on hold cannot be approved: leave it out and say so. Never guess, round or remember a total or a version: if a PO is not in the latest look-up, look it up again. Purchasing approves a PO only when it is still waiting, its total still matches to the cent and its version is the one the look-up returned (a PO that changed since it was looked at is refused); relay its answer as it comes. Not for customer orders.

pos.description: The confirmed vendor POs, one entry each, copied from vendor_po_waiting: {po_number, total_usd, version}.

po_number.description: The PO number from vendor_po_waiting, e.g. 1003.

total_usd.description: That PO's total_usd exactly as vendor_po_waiting returned it.

version.description: Copy version exactly from vendor_po_waiting for that PO.

reason.description: Optional note on the approval, e.g. "approved in chat".

customer_order_lookup.description: Look up customer orders: purchase orders customers (VFC, Gibson, DDA work orders) placed with Dearborn Denim / McMillan Manufacturing. scope=open lists the open customer orders; scope=pipeline shows where they are in production. Read-only. Not for vendor POs.

material_request.description: Ask purchasing to reorder a material (fabric, thread, trims). This does not create a vendor PO: purchasing turns it into a vendor PO draft that Robert approves. If the material name matches several, the reply lists the candidates; ask which one and file again.

material.description: Material as the person names it, e.g. "14oz indigo".

production_lookup.description: Look up production on the factory floor from the piece-work scanner: view=summary for output by operator and operation, view=wip for bundles in progress by stage.

cs_my_queue.description: Your customer-service queue: cs-desk tickets handed to you and waiting on a person (waiting_human), most recently updated first, one line each with the ticket number, customer, subject and when the customer last wrote. Use the ticket number with cs_ticket, then cs_reply.

cs_search.description: Find cs-desk tickets by the customer's email address, an order number or words in the subject or messages, one line each, most recently updated first, any status. Use the ticket number with cs_ticket.

by.description: email = the customer's exact address; order = an order number like #309610; text = words from the subject or the messages.

value.description: The address, order number or words to look for.

cs_ticket.description: Read one customer-service ticket: the header (status, customer, subject) and its last messages, oldest first, with what the customer wrote, what the bot or staff already sent, and internal notes (marked INTERNAL NOTE, never sent to the customer). Always read it before cs_reply.

ticket_id.description: The ticket number, digits only (e.g. 1042 for #1042).

cs_reply.description: Send your reply by email to the customer on a cs-desk ticket, threaded into their conversation; cs-desk adds your signature. Write only the reply body, no signature. Set close=true when nothing more is needed. An email cannot be unsent: it goes out once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

text.description: The reply body exactly as the customer should read it; no signature.

close.description: true = close the ticket after the reply is sent.

cs_note.description: Add an internal note to a cs-desk ticket for Robert and the team (a phone call, what you checked, what is still pending); it is never sent to the customer. Files a request; it runs right away once you are trusted on it, else when Robert approves.

cs_close.description: Close a cs-desk ticket without replying (already answered, resolved, spam or a duplicate). Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

cs_assign_me.description: Take a cs-desk ticket: assign it to yourself so it shows in your queue (cs_my_queue). Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

pickup_status.description: List inbound pickups: goods Dearborn collects at a vendor (a freight carrier, a parcel pickup or our own van) instead of the vendor shipping them. Each has its pickup id, vendor PO number, vendor, mode, state (REQUESTED = waiting on the vendor, READY, BOOKED, PICKED_UP, DELIVERED, MISSED, PROBLEM, CANCELLED, HOLD), ready date, pickup window, quote in USD, whether it is approved, carrier, PRO/tracking and version. status=open (default) lists every pickup not delivered or cancelled; needs_attention the problems, missed runs, holds and quotes waiting for Robert's approval; arriving the booked or picked-up ones due within a week. vendor narrows to one vendor (code or part of the name). Always call this before any other pickup action and use its pickup id, quote and version; never guess them.

vendor.description: Vendor code or part of the vendor name, e.g. "Cone"; leave out for all vendors.

pickup_mark_ready.description: Record that a vendor says the goods for a pickup are ready (or will be on a date), with the piece count, weight and dock hours when known. Get the pickup id from pickup_status. Purchasing then books the pickup when it may. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

ready_on.description: The date the goods are ready, YYYY-MM-DD (today's date if they are ready now).

pieces.description: Cartons, pallets or rolls, when the vendor said.

weight_lb.description: Total weight in pounds, when the vendor said.

pickup_approve.description: Approve the quote of a pickup that is waiting for Robert's approval ("approve the Cone pickup"), so purchasing books it. The rule: first call pickup_status with status=needs_attention, show the person the pickup's vendor, PO number, carrier and quote, and only after they confirm call this with that pickup's id and exactly the quote_usd and version the look-up returned. Never guess, round or remember a quote or a version: if the pickup is not in the latest look-up, look it up again. Purchasing approves only while the pickup is still waiting and unchanged; relay its answer as it comes. A booked pickup cannot be taken back from here.

quote_usd.description: That pickup's quote_usd exactly as pickup_status returned it.

version.description: That pickup's version exactly as pickup_status returned it.

pickup_reschedule.description: Move a pickup to a new day and time window (the vendor asked, the carrier cannot make it, the goods are late). Get the pickup id from pickup_status. A booked pickup stays booked at the new time and the vendor is told. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

hours.description: The new window in Chicago time, HH:MM-HH:MM, e.g. "13:00-16:00".

reason.description: Why it moved, in the person's words.

pickup_collected.description: The driver says the goods of a pickup are loaded on our van ("collected"). Get the pickup id from pickup_status (status=arriving). Receiving still counts them into stock when they arrive. Files a request; it runs once Robert approves (or right away if he has promoted you on it).

pieces.description: How many cartons, pallets or rolls were loaded, when the driver said.

pickup_hold.description: Put a pickup on hold (Robert: "hold the Cone fabric"): it stops where it is (waiting on the vendor, ready, or booked) until it is released, and goes back there on release. Get the pickup id and PO number from pickup_status. Tell the person to let the vendor and carrier know if a truck was booked.

po_number.description: That pickup's vendor PO number from pickup_status.

reason.description: Why it is held, in the person's words.

pickup_release.description: Release a pickup from hold: it goes back to where it was when it was held. Get the pickup id and PO number from pickup_status (status=needs_attention lists holds).

po_number.description: That pickup's vendor PO number from pickup_status.

ops_note.description: Send Robert a note about something on the floor or at the store (a machine down, a delivery problem, a customer issue), or anything you cannot do with your other tools. urgency: fyi, today or now.

text.description: The note, in the person's own words.

ap_aging.description: What Dearborn owes its vendors (accounts payable): open vendor bills captured from invoices emailed to payables@, by how late they are (current = not yet due, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days past due), with a row per vendor and its critical flag. Affiliates (McMillan Manufacturing and the other related companies) are listed apart under intercompany and are never in the totals. Answers "what do we owe". vendor narrows it to one vendor. Read-only; nothing here pays anyone.

vendor.description: Part of a vendor name, e.g. "Cone"; leave out for every vendor.

ap_bills_due.description: List open vendor bills (accounts payable) due before a date, overdue ones included, earliest due first: vendor, invoice number, invoice and due dates, total, balance, PO number, match state (MATCHED, VARIANCE, NO_PO, NO_RECEIPT, DUPLICATE, UNMATCHED_VENDOR), state (CAPTURED, POSTED to QuickBooks, HELD) and days overdue. Answers "what's due this week": pass due_before as the day after the week ends. Read-only; it schedules and pays nothing.

due_before.description: YYYY-MM-DD; bills due before this date. Leave out for every open bill.

vendor.description: Part of a vendor name; leave out for every vendor.

ap_vendor_status.description: One vendor's payables status: open balance and open bills, last payment seen in QuickBooks, its terms and critical/affiliate flags, and kanban POs received with no invoice yet. next_payment is filled only when an approved pay run holds the vendor; when it is empty, promise the vendor no payment date.

name.description: The vendor's name, e.g. "Komar" or "Cranston Trucking".

ap_exceptions.description: The payables exceptions queue: vendor bills that need a person (amount off the PO, no PO, billed before the goods were received, duplicate, vendor not in QuickBooks, low-confidence reading, held, or waiting for extraction), each with its reasons; invoices that failed to read; duplicates refused in the last 30 days; and bills paid from the bank that are still open in QuickBooks. Clearing them happens on the /cfo/ap page. Read-only.
